content.title: From the Cross to the Resurrection - The Most Beautiful Easter Hymns you NEED to Hear!
content.text: "From the Cross to the Resurrection - The Most Beautiful Easter Hymns" - Rosemary Siemens performs 14 of the greatest Easter and Good Friday hymns ever written, with violin, vocals, and piano. Featuring The Old Rugged Cross, Nothing But the Blood of Jesus, Christ the Lord Is Risen Today, He Arose, and more. Perfect for Easter Sunday worship, Good Friday reflection, Holy Week devotions, Lent, Communion, and anyone who needs beautiful peaceful Christian music that tells the full story of Easter — from Calvary to the empty tomb. 0:00 The Old Rugged Cross 6:19 At the Cross (Alas and Did My Savior Bleed) 10:40 Jesus Paid It All 15:03 When I Survey the Wondrous Cross 19:19 At Calvary 23:03 Nothing But the Blood of Jesus 27:13 In the Garden 31:27 I Love to Tell the Story 37:58 My Hope is Built on Nothing Less (On Christ the Solid Rock I Stand) 40:45 I Stand Amazed (O How Marvelous) 44:26 I Will Sing of My Redeemer 49:45 To God Be the Glory 54:35 Christ the Lord Is Risen Today 1:00:09 He Arose (Lo in the Grave He Lay) About This Compilation This collection tells the full story of Easter in hymns - beginning at Calvary and ending at the empty tomb. No other season in the Christian calendar has inspired more hymns of depth and beauty than Holy Week, and these 14 represent some of the finest ever written. The compilation opens at the cross. "The Old Rugged Cross" - written by George Bennard in 1912 - remains one of the most beloved hymns in Christian history. "When I Survey the Wondrous Cross" - written in 1707 by Isaac Watts, often called the Father of English Hymnody - is widely considered one of the greatest hymns ever written. "Nothing But the Blood of Jesus" written by Robert Lowry, who also gave the church "He Arose", asks and answers the most important question in the gospel: what can wash away my sin? "Jesus Paid It All" - with its refrain "sin had left a crimson stain, He washed it white as snow" - is one of the most searched Easter hymns on YouTube. The middle of this compilation is the hinge of Holy Week. "In the Garden" - written by C. Austin Miles in 1912 after a vision of Mary Magdalene at the empty tomb - captures the most intimate moment in the resurrection story. "I Love to Tell the Story" - written by Katherine Hankey in 1866 — captures the response of every believer who has encountered the grace of Easter: an irresistible desire to tell others what Jesus has done. Among the other writers represented: Fanny Crosby, whose "To God Be the Glory" and "I Will Sing of My Redeemer" overflow with resurrection joy; Edward Mote, whose "My Hope Is Built on Nothing Less" - also known as "The Solid Rock" - stands as one of the most enduring declarations of faith ever written; and Charles H. Gabriel, whose "I Stand Amazed in the Presence" captures the personal wonder of a soul that has truly grasped what Easter means. The compilation closes at the empty tomb. "Christ the Lord Is Risen Today" - written in 1739 by Charles Wesley - fills every room with Alleluias. "He Arose" - Robert Lowry's 1874 masterpiece - brings the whole collection home with the most triumphant refrain in Christian music: "Up from the grave He arose, with a mighty triumph o'er His foes." From the cross to the resurrection. From Calvary to the empty tomb. I hope this compilation moves your heart and fills your home with praise. Thanks for helping me Bring Back The Hymns!
